phases.summary: Ternary ISA, assembler, VM widths, integer formats, native ops, and numeric workloads have regression coverage.

SSA IR is the sole target-code source; global optimization, graph coloring/coalescing, iterative spills, ABI v2 compatibility, executable and vector ABI v3 contracts, runtime wrappers, linking, TCL assembly, and dynamic-control JIT lowering have focused coverage. ABI v3 is the release-image default while v2 remains readable and explicitly selectable; the accepted controlled host selects NativeX64Jit by default on x86-64 and retains the cached interpreter elsewhere.
Native kernel, VFS, persistent root image, checkpoint-durable namespace/quota policy, process lifecycle, waits, and app handoff are implemented with production tests.
Host SDL runner boots release images, routes input, decodes framebuffer snapshots, and exports text and PNG diagnostics.
Host tools, manifests, debugging docs, diagnostic bundle contracts, Obsidian vault validation, and Graphify-backed knowledge graph tooling now exist for recursive agent loops.

Synthetic Doom-class and BitNet-style workloads remain the offline defaults; cache-backed Freedoom slice/full rendering and official BitNet slice/full execution are implemented as an explicit manual suite with deterministic hashes and fail-closed missing-cache behavior.
evidence: 2026-08-17 local-cache BitNet slice/full token-hash and two-run reference acceptance

phases.summary: Opt-in host-only TRITENC1 AES-256-GCM envelope parsing, canonical tDisk validation, strict key-file provider, stable inspect/encrypt/decrypt/attach-run lifecycle, atomic replacement, fail-closed provider behavior, and cleanup tests are implemented; release use remains explicitly gated on independent review.
open_items: Resolve nonce uniqueness, replay/rollback, plaintext crash cleanup, key-file race, provider policy, and fuzz coverage findings through the required independent review; any format-affecting remediation requires a new envelope version
Do not close the gap while high-severity review findings remain unresolved

phases.summary: ASCII, UTF-8, and hexadecimal remain compatibility encodings; fixed TASCII-81, exact trits, compact base-27/base-81 notation, allocation-free guest SDK conversions, and backward-compatible symbolic selectors for human and JSON dump surfaces are implemented.

The cross-layer scope is documented for binary device interoperability, physical driver software, TritUI, modular and unikernel profiles, portable vector/matrix acceleration, ACE lowering, and NVFP4 boundaries; these are real future requirements and are not claimed as implemented.
open_items: Define exact-width binary types, endian and packed layouts, byte buffers, MMIO, DMA/coherency, IOMMU, and general interrupt contracts
Define hierarchical device discovery and driver lifecycle, shared virtual devices, and phased physical bus/controller drivers
Promote libwidget into modular TritUI with stable desktop application SDK and accessibility contracts
Define versioned desktop, server, embedded, appliance, and unikernel system profiles with capability closure and reproducible image metadata
Formalize portable vector and matrix semantics before adding future ACE or other hardware lowering
Specify NVFP4 as an explicit tensor compatibility/backend format with conversion and accuracy gates
Defer Qt and Python/TritUI compatibility ports until the native ABI and platform services they consume are stable
